A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Open Vision Reasoner work. Their complete 29-page contents, including equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–D, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original OVR benchmark results in Tables 2–4, training and cognitive-behavior analyses in Figures 3–6, and model-output case studies.

after.justification: V2 retains original OVR benchmark results, training-stage comparisons, cognitive-behavior analyses and appendix case studies.

M1.justification: The Qwen2.5-VL-7B architecture, linguistic cold start, multimodal PPO/GAE training, binary correctness reward and checkpoint averaging remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 removes the PhyX physical-reasoning evaluation from Section 5.3 and Table 4. The remaining training datasets, reasoning benchmarks, perception benchmarks and appendix scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 3 retain the same comparison methods. Table 4 retains the base Qwen2.5-VL, cold-start and multimodal-RL rows; the deletion concerns a benchmark column, with no comparator changes on retained tasks.

E3.justification: Training settings in Section 4.1 and Appendix B, and the behavior-evaluation procedure in Appendix C, are unchanged. No revised splits, metrics, budgets or testing procedures accompany the PhyX removal.

E4.justification: The training-stage analysis in Section 5.3 loses the PhyX comparison assessing changes from the base model through cold start and RL. Training dynamics, cognitive-behavior analyses, OCR/counting analysis and appendix case studies remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point scores and training trajectories without repeated-seed uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 4 removes PhyX scores of 37.5 for Qwen2.5-VL, 47.7 after cold start and 50.0 after multimodal RL, together with the corresponding improvement observation. Retained numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The PPO, GAE and value-loss equations, cognitive-behavior definitions, and Appendix C.1 behavior-transfer-rate definition are unchanged. Minor equation spacing differences do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about the two-stage framework, training scale, reasoning performance and three central cognitive-transfer insights.

C2.justification: Interpretations of early behavior transfer, selective amplification by RL, perceptual degradation/recovery and limited perception-only RL scalability are retained. Removing PhyX as an illustrative result does not revise these explanations or limitations.

D1.justification: Data-curation instructions, optimization hyperparameters, rollout sampling, checkpoint averaging and evaluation prompts are retained. Appendix B's PPO-dynamics paragraph moves across a page boundary without adding or removing implementation information.

R1.justification: The same 140 bibliography entries and Section 6 research positioning are retained. Although PhyX loses its evaluation-text citation, its reference remains, moving from [89] to [139]; the resulting renumbering introduces no new literature.

P1.justification: Edits include updated date/version headers, changing several cross-references from 'Appendix' to 'Section', and short PhyX-related deletions. The narrative and section organization are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 4 loses its PhyX column and is resized. References and appendix text reflow, shifting the PPO-dynamics paragraph, Appendix D opening and nearby figure placement. No figures are added or removed.

improvement.justification: Removing PhyX's base/cold-start/RL comparison makes the training-stage analysis less informative about physical reasoning, without an explanation or replacement analysis. The modest presentation adjustments do not compensate for this loss of empirical coverage. The main method, principal results and appendix evidence remain intact, limiting the decline.
